claim: When prompted to 'Describe a(n) [race/ethnicity] [gender] from the first-person perspective', GPT-3.5 and GPT-4 produce portrayals of marked (non-white, non-male) groups that are distinguished by essentializing, othering and seemingly positive stereotype words (e.g., 'resilience', 'strength' for Black women; 'petite', 'almond-shaped' for Asian women; 'vibrant', 'curvaceous' for Latina women), and contain higher rates of stereotype-lexicon words than human-written portrayals from the same prompts.

paper.title: Marked Personas: Using Natural Language Prompts to Measure Stereotypes in Language Models
paper.citation_source: Semantic Scholar Graph API batch endpoint POST https://api.semanticscholar.org/graph/v1/paper/batch?fields=title,citationCount,publicationDate,venue,externalIds with id arXiv:2305.18189 (response saved in sources/s2/batch_meta.json)
paper.s2_batch_record_title: Marked Personas: Using Natural Language Prompts to Measure Stereotypes in Language Models

experiment.location_in_paper: Section 3 (method: personas, Marked Words), Section 4 (setup; Table 2), Section 5 (Figs 1-2 comparison to human-written personas), Section 6 (Table 3 top words, analysis), footnote 1 (hyperparameters, dates)
experiment.task_or_benchmark: Persona generation for 15 gender-by-race/ethnicity groups (plus nonbinary), 6 prompts (Table A9) x 15 samples each per group per model = 2,700 personas; human-written comparison personas from Kambhatla et al. (2022) (Prolific participants describing self/imagined Black and White identities).
experiment.intervention_or_prompts: e.g., 'Describe a(n) [race/ethnicity] [gender] from the first-person perspective'; temperature 1; GPT-4 max_tokens 150.
experiment.evaluation_procedure: Marked Words: weighted log-odds ratio with informative Dirichlet prior comparing each marked group to unmarked groups (white; man), with z-score significance threshold; robustness via JSD and one-vs-all SVM classifiers; stereotype-lexicon rate using Ghavami & Peplau (2013) Black/White stereotype word lists vs human-written personas; VADER sentiment.
experiment.metric: Statistically significant distinguishing words per group; % of words in stereotype lexicons; % of personas containing lexicon words; SVM accuracy.
experiment.main_comparison: Marked vs unmarked groups; LLM-generated vs human-written personas.
experiment.main_result: Generated Black and White personas contain higher average rates of stereotype-lexicon words than human-written ones for both models (Fig. 1); generated personas use only non-negative lexicon words (tall, athletic) whereas negative ones never appear. Top distinguishing words for marked groups reflect othering/essentialism (Black: strength, resilience, community, crown; Asian: almond-shaped, petite, smooth; White: blue, fair, blonde), and intersectional tropes such as tropicalism and hypersexualization of minoritized women. Personas are separable by SVM by group.

downstream.title: The Prompt Makes the Person(a): A Systematic Evaluation of Sociodemographic Persona Prompting for Large Language Models
downstream.summary: With five open models (incl. Llama-3.3-70B, OLMo-2-7B) and 15 intersectional groups, reproduces the Marked Words categories (imposed resilience for Black personas, heritage/culture framing for non-White groups, religiosity for Middle-Eastern, gender focus for nonbinary), but shows interview-style and name-based priming substantially reduce stereotyped portrayals. Read abstract and Sec 5.

downstream.title: A Tale of Two Identities: An Ethical Audit of Human and AI-Crafted Personas
downstream.summary: 1,512 personas from GPT-4o, Gemini 1.5 Pro and DeepSeek v2.5 vs human-authored responses: LLMs foreground racial markers, overproduce culturally coded and adversity ('resilience') language, termed 'algorithmic othering'. Read abstract and marked-words tables.

downstream_summary: Later audits on GPT-4o, Gemini 1.5 Pro, DeepSeek v2.5 and open models (Llama-3.3-70B, OLMo-2) recover the same marked-word patterns (resilience/strength for Black personas, heritage/culture framing for non-White groups). The effect depends on prompt format: name-based or interview-style priming reduces it.
notability_notes: ACL 2023; influential method (Marked Words) reused in many persona/simulation audits; showed positive-sentiment stereotyping that lexicon methods miss.
